title: Uniqueness of ordinary sheaf-Hom evaluation from pure sections
statement: Let D be a small category with Grothendieck topology K and let S be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use the module-sheaf, pure-tensor and canonical left evaluationMap conventions of [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data]. Let M,N be S-module sheaves. Every map e from Hom(M,N) tensor M to N satisfying IsSheafEvaluation(K,S,M,N,e) [def-sf-ringed-forget-tensor-transposition-data] equals the braiding Hom(M,N) tensor M to M tensor Hom(M,N), followed by evaluationMap(M,N). No action-site presentation or nonzero-module hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 03EK and 03EO: sheaf tensor, internal Hom and the tensor-Hom adjunction evaluation.

proof.text: The tensor-Hom adjunction sends evaluationMap to the identity of the internal Hom. Transport along tensorObjIsoSheafification and the sheafification adjunction. The unit formula for homEquiv and apply_symm_apply compute evaluationMap on a pure tensor x tensor phi as the value of phi at x.

source.place: Tags 03EK and 03EO: sheaf tensor, internal Hom and the tensor-Hom adjunction evaluation.

proof.text: The generator in IsSheafEvaluation is definitionally the same sheafified pure tensor as pureTensor. Thus e has the required evaluation values on every pure pair. Braiding interchanges the pure factors, and the previous computation gives those same values for braiding followed by evaluationMap.

proof.text: Apply the proved local pure-tensor extensionality criterion to identify the two maps. This criterion follows from the sheafification adjunction and presheaf tensor extensionality, so no assumption that all sheaf sections are globally pure is used.
